name: DefiPlaza
rootCause: The vulnerability lies in the removeLiquidity function of the DefiPlaza contract. Specifically, it involved a rounding error when inputting a LPamount that exceeded 15/16ths of the total LP amount. For sufficiently large input fractions, F_ it will be rounded down to zero at line 322. The result of this rounding error is that all liquidity for this token was removed Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://app.blocksec.com/explorer/tx/eth/0xa245deda8553c6e4c575baff9b50ef35abf4c8f990f8f36897696f896f240e3a Analysis: https://defiplaza.net/blog/post-mortem-of-defiplaza-ethereum-exploit/

descriptions.text: The vulnerability lies in the removeLiquidity function of the DefiPlaza contract. Specifically, it involved a rounding error when inputting a LPamount that exceeded 15/16ths of the total LP amount. For sufficiently large input fractions, F_ it will be rounded down to zero at line 322. The result of this rounding error is that all liquidity for this token was removed Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://app.blocksec.com/explorer/tx/eth/0xa245deda8553c6e4c575baff9b50ef35abf4c8f990f8f36897696f896f240e3a Analysis: https://defiplaza.net/blog/post-mortem-of-defiplaza-ethereum-exploit/

DefiPlaza’s Ethereum deployment was drained on July 5, 2024 after an attacker exploited a precision loss bug in the removeLiquidity path. The exploit used large flash loans to gain dominant LP ownership, emptied the ETH side of the pool through a rounding condition, then drained remaining assets with sequential near-zero swaps. An MEV bot front ran the original attacker and captured the exploit transaction first. A rounding error in DefiPlaza V2’s removeLiquidity logic allowed a liquidity-removal fraction greater than 15/16 of the total LP supply to round a token balance factor down to zero.
